lots.title: Repairs and/or modification to metal items
lots.description: Lot 1 covers repairs and/or modification to metal items under Bristol City Council's Metal Works Dynamic Purchasing System. The DPS Agreement body provides only the lot title and a short scope label; detailed product-level specification, performance requirements and KPIs are deferred to the Call-Off competition stage (per Schedule 1 wording 'AS SPECIFIED IN ANY CALL FOR FURTHER COMPETITION IN RESPECT OF THE LOTS FOR WHICH THE PROVIDER IS ADMITTED TO THE DPS' and Schedule 7 / Order Form Appendix 1 references).
requirements: Provider must comply with all DPS Agreement obligations including the General Terms and Conditions, statutory requirements (Clause 11), and call-off ordering procedure (Clause 13).

Provider must maintain the cross-cutting insurance minimums for each Call-Off Contract: Employer's Liability £10M each and every claim, Public Liability £5M each and every claim (uplift possible per call-off), Professional Indemnity £2.5M each and every claim (uplift possible per call-off).

Detailed lot-specific scope (deliverables, milestones, KPIs, Goods/Services/Works requirements) is set in the Call-Off Order Form (Appendix 1) and the Specification attached at Appendix 1 to the Order Form, and is not enumerated in the DPS Agreement body.

evaluation_criteria.summary: Schedule 2 (AWARD CRITERIA) contains an empty quality criteria/weighting table for DPS establishment and explicitly tags the selection step as 'Pas91 Pass/Fail', i.e. PAS 91 pre-qualification questionnaire on a pass/fail basis. No quantitative weightings are populated in the DPS Agreement body.

warnings.message: Document is the DPS Agreement template (Metal-Works-DPS-Final-Draft); Schedule 1 (THE SERVICES AND/OR WORKS SPECIFICATION) explicitly defers detailed product/technical requirements to the call-off competition stage ('AS SPECIFIED IN ANY CALL FOR FURTHER COMPETITION'). No concrete product items, materials, dimensions or per-lot technical standards are present in the document body, so product_requirement_seeds is empty and per-lot product_requirements arrays are empty. Detail must be sourced from per-call-off ITTs or other contract documents on ProContract.
evidence_refs: line:218 (Schedule 1 – THE SERVICES AND/OR WORKS SPECIFICATION)
line:1027 (Order Form Appendix 1: 'as set out in the Specification attached at Appendix 1')

warnings.message: Schedule 2 (Award Criteria) contains an empty quality criteria/weightings table for DPS establishment; only the selection-stage 'Pas91 Pass/Fail' tag is populated. Schedule 3 (Pricing Matrices) is annotated 'NOT REQUIRED UNTIL CALL FOR FURTHER COMPETITION STAGE'. Per-lot evaluation criteria with quantitative weightings are therefore not extractable from this document.

No CPV codes are present in the DPS Agreement body. Process-level CPV signals (44221300-8 Gates, 44400000-4 Miscellaneous fabricated products, 45223100-7 Assembly of metal structures) come from process_context only; they are NOT asserted by this document and have not been replicated into per-lot cpv_codes arrays. The daemon may inherit them from the contract notice if its policy permits, but this skill does not authoritatively map them to lots.

Per-lot descriptions in the DPS Agreement body consist solely of lot titles repeated in three places (cover-page heading list at lines 9-17, BACKGROUND clause 1 at line 39, and BACKGROUND clause 3 at line 41). The document does NOT include per-lot scope paragraphs, examples, quantities or sites. The richer per-lot descriptions found in the existing notice_lots rows (e.g. 'examples: lockers for parking meters, water taps, signs, and specialist artwork' for Lot 3) originate from notice metadata, not from this DPS Agreement document.

Docling extraction reports page_count = 0 in document_extractions; evidence_anchor.page_ref values therefore use markdown line numbers ('line:N') rather than physical page numbers. Downstream consumers should treat page_ref as a logical anchor into the extracted markdown, not a paginated PDF coordinate.

BS EN 15713:2009 is mentioned in Appendix 3 (Data Processing) for secure destruction of personal data at end of contract. It is a data-handling standard, not a metalworks technical standard, and applies to the contract overall rather than to any individual lot. It has been deliberately omitted from per-lot technical_standards arrays to avoid misclassifying it as a product/installation standard.
